mira: Hey team — escalation from AcmeCorp. Customer sees UI error when confirming billing: "Payment failed. Please try again." No request ID shown in the UI. Happened ~2026-03-16 15:42 UTC. Screenshot attached. Can you confirm what we need to repro?

devon: Thanks. Primary ask: we need a HAR + console logs from the user's browser and a copy-as-cURL for the failed network call (if present). Also exact local time and steps the user took. Which browser/OS did they use?

mira: They say Chrome on macOS Ventura, latest stable. Steps: 1) Sign in -> Billing -> Select Team Standard -> Click "Confirm payment" -> spinner -> error. No redirect. User email: fran@acme.example. No visible request-id in UI.

devon: OK. Ask them to capture Chrome HAR + console. Quick steps to paste for the customer:
- Open Chrome DevTools (Cmd+Option+I) -> Network tab.
- Check "Preserve log" and optionally "Disable cache".
- Reproduce the issue (click Confirm payment).
- Right-click any request and choose "Save all as HAR with content" -> attach the .har here.
- To get console: Console tab -> right-click -> "Save as..." (or copy visible error text). Make sure to reproduce while DevTools is open so JS errors are captured.

devon: If they want to give a single quick copy of the failing request: in Network tab -> find the request to our billing endpoint (filter by "/v1/payments" or "/payments") -> right click -> Copy -> "Copy as cURL (bash)". That gives us exact headers + body.

devon: Important: redact any full credit card numbers or raw tokens before sending. For the HAR: open in text editor and replace Authorization header value and cookie values with "REDACTED". We mainly need: response status code, response body (if not PII), and request/response headers including any "x-redwood-request-id" or "x-request-id" we can use to look up server logs.

mira: Can you paste a tiny example we can include in the customer's instructions so they can run a quick local curl repro?

devon: Sure — include this snippet as an example (note: replace body/ids as needed):

```
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payments' \
  -H 'Authorization: REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.5' \
  --data '{"amount":1999,"currency":"usd","method":"card","metadata":{"email":"fran@acme.example"}}'
```

devon: If they paste the full "Copy as cURL" output, we can run it internally (after redaction) to reproduce. Also ask them to note any status code in the network row (e.g., 4xx/5xx) and copy the response body.

jordan: A few extras we always request:
- exact local timestamp (time zone) when they reproduced,
- the HAR file,
- console logs (full),
- the "copy as cURL" for the failing request if available,
- whether they were on Team Dedicated or Hosted (affects routing).

support-bot: :warning: If the HAR/console contains PII (payment method details, SSNs), redact before upload. Use the internal redaction guide: https://redwood.internal/docs/redact-har (customer-facing link to be replaced).

mira: Great. What about Firefox differences? Customer sometimes uses Firefox.

devon: Firefox steps are similar: DevTools -> Network -> check "Persist Logs" -> reproduce -> right-click -> "Save All As HAR". Console -> right-click -> "Export Visible Messages to file". Edge follows Chrome steps. Safari: Web Inspector -> Network timeline export.

mira: I'll send this to the customer now. One more Q: how do they find the x-request-id in the HAR?

devon: In the HAR JSON, search for "headers" of the request/response entries. Look for header names: "x-redwood-request-id" or "x-request-id". In DevTools you can also click the request -> Headers -> Response Headers and look for the header. If they share that ID, give it to us and we can search the server logs directly.

mira: Perfect — thanks. I'll upload whatever they send to this thread. :pray:

support-bot: automated-note: If you attach >1MB files, please use the support upload portal or dropbox link — thread attachments may get truncated.

mira: Uploaded: acme_payment_fail.har and console_log_2026-03-16.txt (redacted). Sending x-redwood-request-id: rwd_9b8f2c1a.

devon: Got it — pulling logs now. Thanks!
